reasoning: R9 fixes all three R8 blockers with board-only changes. The shot builder is now event-aware, so every event finishes inside the shot whose view performs it. That restores B's signature second-lens crossing, B's opening pull-back and the s6 path spread in both treatments. The s7 narration lost one word and its tag event moved earlier, which brings the scene and both reward intervals inside the limits under a slow envelope built from measured maxima. My own arithmetic confirms each figure, and the boundaries still hold when I rescale the scene fractions to the fast and slow envelopes. The one script change keeps the required attribution chain: the university reports early validation of the chip AI, and the accuracy figure follows. I record two wording concerns for the required fresh source validation rather than as blockers. R7-5 is resolved at plan level. No blocker remains, so the verdict is pass. concerns: Splitting the metric across two sentences ('...chip AI validation.' / 'Accuracy was ...') makes sentence 12, read as its own caption, an unqualified accuracy figure, and a lay listener may hear sentence 11's 'validation' as 'validated'. Sentence 13's field limit and the on-screen validation card and tag mitigate this. The independent source validator should rule on it explicitly. If it objects, any rewording that restores 'Validation accuracy' must keep s7 at 21 words or fewer, or re-check the 9.5 s slow ceiling.

The s7 slow margin is 0.08 s. A read slower than the measured maxima could put s7 past 9.5 s after measured retime. The fix would be board-only, a scene split, but it would need another reboard and review.
The projection assumes a 0.30 s lead, while take 5's first word was at 0.58 s. That shifts every time by about 0.28 s. It doesn't break any limit I checked.
